summary:
"Earth in Sound" is an interactive web application that transforms NASA scientific visualization videos into music. It analyzes video frames using computer vision techniques, extracting visual features such as brightness and changes between frames. These features are mapped to musical parameters, including pitch, rhythm, and volume, allowing users to experience scientific data through sound.

The application currently supports three NASA visualizations: solar activity, nitrogen dioxide concentrations, and precipitation. Users can explore each visualization while customizing the musical experience through instrument selection, tempo, pitch range, and volume controls.

Earth in Sound offers an alternative way to interact with scientific information, making complex visual data more engaging and accessible through sonification.
details:
Earth in Sound is an interactive web application that transforms NASA scientific visualizations into music. Its primary goal is to demonstrate that scientific data can be perceived not only visually but also through sound, opening up new ways to engage with information and making the exploration of such data more compelling.
The application analyzes video frames, extracting visual characteristics—such as brightness and frame-to-frame changes—which a specialized algorithm then converts into musical parameters, including pitch, rhythm, and volume. Users can select different visualizations and customize the sound by adjusting the tempo, the musical instrument, and other settings. The project features three NASA visualizations: solar activity, nitrogen oxide concentrations, and precipitation.
By offering an alternative way to perceive scientific information, the project makes data interaction more dynamic and allows users to explore data from a unique perspective. Earth in Sound is intended to help popularize NASA’s scientific visualizations, introduce people to the concept of sonification, and spark interest in novel methods of data representation.
The development process utilized Python, OpenCV, NumPy, and SciPy for video analysis and data processing; Flask for the backend; React and TypeScript for the user interface; and the Web Audio API for sound generation and playback. Additionally, Google AI Studio, GitHub, and Render were used throughout the development lifecycle.
